[control: no-repeat]
[motif: A–C–B. Rising minor third, falling semitone. Three notes, quarter-note triplet in 3/4.]
[Intro | 16 bars | 3/4 | piano and marimba in exact octave unison]
[motif stated four times unaltered | bass and guitar double | drums weight every beat equally]
[Verse 1 | duet alternating | tenor and alto | near-spoken | piano and bass only]
[male tenor vocal] You have a Bronco?
[female alto vocal] Yeah. Seventy-two.
[male tenor vocal] No kidding. We have the same car.
[female alto vocal] We don't have the same car.
[male tenor vocal] Same year, same model, same color.
[female alto vocal] Where's yours?
[male tenor vocal] Outside.
[female alto vocal] So is mine.
[male tenor vocal] Then we have two cars.
[female alto vocal] Apparently language has one.
[Interlude | 32 bars | 3/4 | strict tempo | marimba leads]
[bars 1-16: motif in exact unison, piano marimba bass guitar woodwind all on the same pitches]
[bars 17-22: repetition holds, drums begin accenting beat 2 instead of beat 1]
[bars 23-32: marimba plays B–C–A, retrograde, same three pitches reversed, nothing else changes]
[Verse 2 | duet alternating | dry restrained | piano and brushed drums]
[male tenor vocal] We went to the same school.
[female alto vocal] What year?
[male tenor vocal] Eighty-nine.
[female alto vocal] I got there in '04.
[male tenor vocal] Same school.
[female alto vocal] Mine had lockers down the east hall.
[male tenor vocal] Mine didn't have an east hall.
[female alto vocal] Different building, then.
[male tenor vocal] The sign out front hasn't changed.
[female alto vocal] So we went to the same sign.
[Interlude | 32 bars | motivic transformation | piano leads, guitar and woodwind answer]
[piano states motif at pitch, guitar states it inverted A–F#–G, woodwind transposes it up a fourth]
[same interval content in all three, no two share a note]
[bars 9, 17, 25: one 5/4 measure each, waltz motion continues through them]
[marimba holds the original pitches underneath, unchanged, increasingly wrong against everything above]
[Verse 3 | duet alternating | slightly more pointed | bass and marimba only]
[male tenor vocal] We believe the same thing.
[female alto vocal] All right. Say it.
[male tenor vocal] I just did.
[female alto vocal] Say what you believe.
[male tenor vocal] Everybody should follow the same rule.
[female alto vocal] The same rule should apply to everybody.
[male tenor vocal] Right. Same thing.
[female alto vocal] Is it?
[male tenor vocal] You know what I mean.
[female alto vocal] I thought I did.
[Interlude | 40 bars | imitative counterpoint | four independent voices | no doubling]
[piano leads, guitar enters two bars later at the fifth, woodwind enters inverted, bass enters in augmentation at half speed]
[bars 1-16: all four consonant, harmonic destination agreed]
[bars 17-28: guitar phrases in 5/4 against piano in 3/4, bar lines stop coinciding]
[bars 29-40: voices choose different tonics, A minor against C major, controlled dissonance, no resolution]
[Verse 4 | duet alternating | accompaniment nearly absent | single sustained bass note]
[male tenor vocal] I'm the same person I was.
[female alto vocal] As when?
[male tenor vocal] Before all this.
[female alto vocal] Pick a year.
[male tenor vocal] Any year.
[female alto vocal] Same person?
[male tenor vocal] Same name, mostly.
[female alto vocal] Same body?
[male tenor vocal] I wouldn't swear to a cell.
[female alto vocal] Then what's the same?
[male tenor vocal] The pronoun.
[Outro | 48 bars | all transformations at once | full ensemble]
[bars 1-12: original, retrograde, inversion and augmentation sound simultaneously in different phrase lengths]
[bars 13-20: 7/8 measures, the waltz nearly loses its footing]
[bars 21-28: everything converges, tempo steadies, apparent return to rigid 3/4 unison]
[bars 29-48: exact unison achieved except marimba, holding one altered pitch]
[final measure: 4/4, one extra beat, full ensemble stop on the downbeat]
[End]
style: Art Rock, Avant-Prog jazz-rock chamber ensemble at 92 BPM, an unstable waltz fracturing from rigid 3/4 into 5/4 and 7/8; piano, electric guitar, bass, drums, marimba, woodwinds and occasional brass develop a three-note motif through unison, retrograde, inversion, augmentation, polymeter and controlled dissonance, Two understated male tenor and female alto voices trade near-spoken, articulate English dialogue with sparse dry treatment between 16–32-bar instrumental developments, Dry detailed mix, strong separation, dynamic ensemble playing, harmonic drift, increasingly pointed restraint.

review.review_text: The joke here is philosophical, and Rose plays it straight the whole way through. Two voices, a tenor and an alto, trade near-spoken lines over a waltz that keeps threatening to fall apart: piano and marimba lock into a three-note figure at the top, then the marimba quietly refuses to change while everything above it drifts, splinters into 5/4, and finally staggers through a few bars of 7/8 where the meter nearly loses its footing entirely. The whole record is an argument about sameness that keeps dissolving under its own logic. "We have the same car," he offers; "we don't have the same car," she answers, and by the closing verse the only thing left that's identical is the pronoun. It's structurally the most ambitious thing in his catalog since 'Outlandia,' and if the payoff lives in the design more than in any single hook, that's the point: the marimba holding one wrong note under a full-ensemble unison is worth the wait. A grower, and one for listeners who want to hear the seams.
